source.title: A Deeper Analysis of Block-Sparse Featurizers

page_placements.theme: Manifold tiling: continuous features split across many localized latents or blocks

record.tranche_reason: The study reports feature splitting in block-sparse featurizers (BSFs), not the size-dependent SAE behavior specified by the claim versions. Its BSF results are recorded as related findings that fit no version.
record.gate_note: The reported SAE comparison concerns reconstruction recovery, not size-dependent SAE feature splitting. The size sweep, sparsity sweep, seed analyses, and Tournament Top-K results concern BSFs. The paper also reports that most features split across multiple blocks in brief DINOv3/CLIP experiments.
record.test_reason: The study's splitting is one synthetic manifold feature divided across 2+ blocks of a fixed-capacity block-sparse featurizer (BSF). That is a different construct from any version. No version's behaviour is measured by SAE dictionary size, parent-child families, absorption, cross-size latent decomposition, or Matryoshka-vs-standard SAE splitting. The block-count sweep (G=128/256/512) concerns BSFs, and the authors frame it as testing whether hyperparameters cause splitting, not whether coarse features refine. The only SAE result (Table 1) is reconstruction recovery against BSF. The Matryoshka SAEs trained in §6 report no splitting results.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors also state that BSF splitting occurs at a smaller rate than SAE manifold tiling. They say they do not fully understand why splits form.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses top-k Grassmannian block-sparse featurizers with learned subspace frames, rather than comparing SAE dictionaries of increasing size. Its central data are synthetic manifolds, with only brief BSF experiments on real vision models.
record.method_sensitivity: In the BSF experiments, splitting persists across block counts G = 128, 256, 512; increasing top-k from 4 to 8 worsens recovery and at 8 no feature is captured by one block. Tournament Top-K reduces splitting in the correlated dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: BSFs split some manifold features across 2 blocks (otherwise >8) even on independent data. This persists across G=128/256/512 and gets worse with top-k from 4 to 8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Block-sparse featurizers split single manifold features across blocks independent of data correlation or block count.

fits_no_version.finding: Split block pairs (n=83) converge to near-orthogonal complements of the same feature. AuxK and k-annealing do not significantly drive the splitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BSF splits are orthogonal decompositions of one manifold rather than regional tiling.

fits_no_version.finding: Tournament Top-K raises the fraction of well-recovered manifolds from 0.77 to 0.90 on the correlated Manifold Zoo.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A selection rule penalizing overlapping blocks reduces BSF splitting.

fits_no_version.finding: In DINOv3/CLIP BSFs, most preset features were split across multiple blocks for causal ablation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BSF feature splitting also appears in real vision models.

record.problems: Most splitting analyses use a synthetic Manifold Zoo. The real-model section is explicitly brief, and it does not provide model-specific splitting results. Several quantitative details appear only in figures; uncertainty estimates are not stated.

untested.parts: No SAE dictionary-size sweep, and no check that finer latents cover a coarse latent's inputs or lie near its direction.
No SAE splitting results in large models or open SAE releases. Real-model work is BSF-only and brief.
No nested or hierarchical feature families. The synthetic features are independent manifolds with no hierarchy.
No parent/child latents and no absorption measurement. Absorption is only mentioned as a known SAE problem.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, and no novel-latent analysis.
No test of whether SAE-objective splitting reflects model units. Matryoshka SAEs were trained (§6), but no splitting comparison is reported.

record.verdict_notes: The record's not-tested judgment holds. Table 1 (SAE vs BSF recovery R2, 0.36 to 0.77) is a method comparison and correctly left out. The §5 feature-merging result (up to three linear features in one block) is also unrelated to any version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test increasing SAE dictionary size or whether larger-SAE features partition a smaller-SAE feature's inputs and lie near its direction.
Brief BSF experiments on vision models are not tests of the stated pattern in large models or open SAE releases.
Does not test nested, geometrically close SAE feature families that mirror a hierarchy of concepts.
Does not test parent-child SAE firing, absorption, or whether SAE size or sparsity changes fix absorption.
Does not test decompositions between larger- and smaller-SAE latents or whether SAE dictionaries add novel latents.
Does not test whether SAE-objective splitting reflects model units, or whether Matryoshka SAEs change or reduce SAE splitting.

rows.subject: BSF
rows.operation_detail: Matched each toy feature to the block with the highest firing correlation and measured feature recovery R2.
rows.measure: Per-feature recovery R2 using one block
rows.value: Segments, spheres, helices, and tori were almost always well recovered by one block; other concept manifolds flickered from seed to seed.
rows.note: Reports BSF recovery and seed variation, not SAE dictionary-size splitting.

rows.subject: BSF
rows.operation_detail: Counted the blocks needed for each feature to reach R2 > 0.8.
rows.measure: Number of blocks per feature to reach R2 > 0.8
rows.value: The answer was either 1, 2, or more than 8 (counted as not recovered); every concept was captured by exactly one block in at least one of the 10 seeds.
rows.note: Aggregate description; no per-feature counts are given in the text.

rows.subject: BSF
rows.operation_detail: Repeated the 10-seed feature-recovery and splitting analysis.
rows.measure: Feature recovery R2 and splitting patterns
rows.value: Results were described as having similar R2 scores and similar feature-splitting patterns to the independent-dataset experiment.
rows.note: No numeric per-feature values are stated in the text.

rows.subject: BSF
rows.operation_detail: Swept the number of BSF blocks.
rows.value: Splitting persisted in every setting, including G = M = 128.
rows.note: This is a BSF block-count sweep, not a sweep of SAE dictionary size.
rows.check: Row is correct as a BSF finding. Do not read it as V1: it is a block-count sweep in which one feature splits across blocks, not coarse-to-fine refinement of SAE latents.

rows.subject: BSF
rows.value: Performance degraded as k increased; at k = 8, not a single feature was captured by one block.
rows.note: The text gives the qualitative trend and the k = 8 outcome, not exact recovery values.

rows.subject: BSF
rows.value: AuxK was not found to significantly contribute to block splitting.

rows.subject: BSF
rows.value: k-annealing was not found to significantly contribute to block splitting.

rows.subject: BSF
rows.operation_detail: Tracked the geometric overlap and feature-firing correlations of split block pairs during training.
rows.measure: Subspace overlap and each block's firing correlation with the feature
rows.value: Pairs began specializing on the same feature around epoch 3; their overlap was around 0.3 for a while, then they ended up as almost orthogonal components of the feature.
rows.note: The authors describe the pair components as near-orthogonal complements, unlike the nearby directions specified in the claim.
rows.check: Split block pairs end as near-orthogonal complements (overlap ~0.3 mid-training, against a ~0.15 random baseline). This is unlike V1/V3's nearby directions, but it is a BSF construct, so no version link.

rows.subject: BSF
rows.measure: Mean recovery R2 and fraction of well-recovered manifolds
rows.value: Tournament Top-K raised mean recovery R2 significantly and the fraction of well-recovered manifolds to 0.90.
rows.note: The paper says splitting is significantly reduced, not eliminated; no numeric mean R2 is stated in the text.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method (Tournament Top-K) with plain top-k: 0.77 to 0.90 well-recovered. It is a method-performance row, not a measure of splitting arising in a standard SAE.

rows.subject: DINOv3 and CLIP BSFs (aggregate; model-specific results not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Ablated and injected blocks on labeled external data to assess feature causality.
rows.measure: Number of blocks needed to observe feature causality
rows.value: Most features were split among multiple blocks, so the authors had to ablate across quite a few blocks at once to observe causality.
rows.note: The result is reported collectively; the text does not assign it separately to DINOv3 or CLIP.
rows.check: The subject is aggregate DINOv3/CLIP BSFs. It gives no count or rate, only that most features needed multi-block ablation. Keep as unquantified.

relation.reason: It draws an analogy to SAE manifold tiling and does not test any version.

tranche.reason: BSF block splitting of synthetic manifold features is a different construct from SAE dictionary-size splitting. The study offers an analogy and a fix for its own method.

source_check.notes: BSF splitting is a block-level analogue of SAE splitting, not SAE dictionary-size splitting. The authors say it occurs at a smaller rate than SAE tiling. The 0.77 in Table 1 (BSF mean recovery R2) is a different number from the 0.77 well-recovered fraction in Figure 12.

statements.correction: Per feature and seed, the blocks needed to reach R2 > 0.8 are 1, 2, or more than 8 (Fig 4). More than 8 is counted as not recovered, not as a split. When a feature splits, it is almost always across exactly 2 blocks (§3.4). Splitting persists at G=128/256/512 (Fig 7). Sweeping k in {4,6,8} degrades performance as k rises, and at k=8 every feature splits across blocks (Fig 8). On the correlated dataset, Tournament Top-K lifts the fraction of well-recovered manifolds from 0.77 to 0.90 (Fig 12).
statements.problem: '(otherwise >8)' presents more than 8 blocks as a split count. The paper counts >8 blocks as not recovered within 8, and says splits are almost always exactly 2 blocks.
